title: Grainfall by SnowHeadStudio
author: Old-Shift-7030
selftext:
This is Grainfall, a falling-block puzzle I’ve been building in Godot 4.7.

The twist: when a piece lands, it doesn’t stay a block. It dissolves into dry sand that slides and piles up for real. You don’t clear lines; you clear a colour that connects from the left wall to the right wall. Chain clears for combos.

The sand simulation is a C++ GDExtension (about 70k grains on a 160×432 grid, fixed 60 Hz tick) ON ANY DEVICE., and Godot draws it with a small shader.

It’s fully deterministic: every round can be replayed tick by tick, and the replay is checked against state hashes, on Windows and on the web.

The sand is tuned to behave like real dry sand. It drifts slightly toward grains of its own colour, but subtly enough that you shouldn’t notice.

It’s a closed pre-alpha and runs in the browser. I’d love feedback on how the sand feels. Does it read as satisfying, or as chaos?

"tsk tsk i used genai for coding but not that heavily"
